packet.headline_seed: Why a Diljit Dosanjh film vanished from streaming after two days
packet.description_seed: The film's troubled journey spans years of censorship disputes, court battles and an unexpected release on a streaming platform.

what: Why a Diljit Dosanjh film vanished from streaming after two days

clean_source_blocks.text: The film's troubled journey spans years of censorship disputes, court battles and an unexpected release on a streaming platform.

What was supposed to be Diljit Dosanjh's long-awaited comeback turned into another controversy within 48 hours. Here's why Satluj was pulled from OTT and the true story that made it one of India's most debated films. Diljit Dosanjh's long-delayed film ‘Satluj’ has once again found itself at the centre of controversy. After years of battling certification issues, title changes, and release delays, the film finally premiered on ZEE5 on July 3, 2026 only to be removed from the platform in India less than 48 hours later. The film, directed by Honey Trehan and starring Diljit Dosanjh as slain human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, remains available on ZEE5 Global outside India, while its future domestic release remains uncertain. On July 5, ZEE5 announced that ‘Satluj’ had been taken down from its Indian catalogue, citing only "current developments" without elaborating further.

The title changed more than once because the makers could not secure approval for the original name, Ghallughara, and later the censorship process pushed the film toward the title Punjab 95. After years of delay, the film finally arrived on streaming as Satluj, with Honey Trehan saying the earlier titles could not be retained. He also made it clear that the team refused to release a compromised version. Even after finally releasing on ZEE5 Global, the film was reportedly taken down from the platform in India shortly after it began streaming. That sudden removal sparked fresh discussion about censorship, political pressure and the unresolved conflict surrounding the film’s content. The film had already faced heavy delays, a withdrawn festival premiere, and years of uncertainty before its release.

Diljit Dosanjh plays human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra in Satluj The abrupt removal of a film starring popular Indian singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh from a streaming platform has triggered a row. Satluj is inspired by the life of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, who investigated allegations of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings during Punjab's separatist insurgency - and then he himself disappeared. He was later found to have been abducted and murdered. Several Punjab police officers were eventually convicted for their role in the killing. Satluj was released on the ZEE5 platform on Friday but removed two days later. ZEE5 said in a statemen, externalt the film would be unavailable in India "until further notice" because of "current developments" but did not explain what they were. With ZEE5 pulling it, the film is no longer officially available in India.

He was later found to have been abducted and murdered. Several Punjab police officers were eventually convicted for their role in the killing.

ZEE5 said in a statemen, externalt the film would be unavailable in India "until further notice" because of "current developments" but did not explain what they were.

With ZEE5 pulling it, the film is no longer officially available in India.

Completed in 2022, the film never made it to cinemas because of a prolonged dispute with India's film certification board.

payload.title: Diljit Dosanjhin Satluj-elokuva poistui Intian suoratoistosta kahdessa päivässä
payload.summary: Intialaisen laulaja-näyttelijä Diljit Dosanjhin tähdittämä Satluj ehti olla katsottavissa ZEE5-palvelussa Intiassa vain noin kaksi päivää ennen kuin se poistettiin maan katalogista. Elokuvan taustalla on vuosia jatkunut kiista sensuurista, nimenmuutoksista ja julkaisun viivästymisestä.
payload.content:
Intialaisen laulaja-näyttelijä Diljit Dosanjhin tähdittämä Satluj on poistettu ZEE5-suoratoistopalvelun Intian valikoimasta vain noin kaksi päivää julkaisunsa jälkeen. Elokuva kertoo ihmisoikeusaktivisti Jaswant Singh Khalrasta, ja sen tie yleisön nähtäväksi on ollut poikkeuksellisen vaikea: vuosien aikana sitä ovat varjostaneet sertifiointikiistat, nimenmuutokset, peruttu festivaaliesitys ja epävarmuus kotimaan julkaisusta.

## Elokuva katosi Intian valikoimasta

Satluj julkaistiin ZEE5-palvelussa perjantaina 3. heinäkuuta 2026. Jo 5. heinäkuuta palvelu ilmoitti, että elokuva on poistettu Intian katalogista. Yhtiön mukaan elokuva ei ole maassa saatavilla toistaiseksi ”nykyisten kehityskulkujen” vuoksi, mutta tarkempaa syytä ei kerrottu.

Poisto on herättänyt Intiassa uuden kiistan sensuurista, poliittisesta paineesta ja siitä, miksi elokuvan sisältö on ollut vuosien ajan niin kiistanalainen. Elokuva on yhä saatavilla ZEE5 Global -palvelussa Intian ulkopuolella, mutta sen kotimaan tulevaisuus on epävarma. Kun ZEE5 poisti teoksen Intian valikoimasta, Satluj ei enää ole virallisesti katsottavissa Intiassa.

## Taustalla Jaswant Singh Khalran tapaus

Honey Trehanin ohjaama elokuva on saanut innoituksensa Jaswant Singh Khalran elämästä. Khalra tutki väitteitä pakotetuista katoamisista ja lain ulkopuolisista surmista Punjabin separatistisen kapinan aikana. Myöhemmin hän itse katosi, ja hänen todettiin joutuneen siepatuksi ja murhatuksi. Useita Punjabin poliiseja tuomittiin lopulta heidän roolistaan surmassa.

Elokuvan nimi on vaihtunut useammin kuin kerran. Alkuperäiseksi nimeksi kaavailtua Ghallugharaa ei saatu hyväksyttyä, ja sensuuriprosessin aikana elokuvaa vietiin kohti nimeä Punjab 95. Lopulta se julkaistiin suoratoistossa nimellä Satluj. Ohjaaja Trehanin mukaan aiempia nimiä ei voitu säilyttää, ja tekijät kieltäytyivät julkaisemasta kompromissiversiota.

Satlujin nopea poistaminen Intiassa jatkaa elokuvan pitkää ja hankalaa julkaisuhistoriaa. Tapaus on noussut jälleen esimerkiksi siitä, miten poliittisesti herkkä aihe voi vaikuttaa elokuvan levitykseen vielä sen jälkeenkin, kun se on viimein päässyt yleisön saataville.
summary_bullets: Satluj poistettiin ZEE5:n Intian valikoimasta noin kaksi päivää julkaisunsa jälkeen.
Elokuva kertoo ihmisoikeusaktivisti Jaswant Singh Khalrasta, jonka tapaus liittyy Punjabin levottomuuksien aikaan.
ZEE5 viittasi poistossa ”nykyisiin kehityskulkuihin”, mutta ei avannut syytä tarkemmin.

The film's troubled journey spans years of censorship disputes, court battles and an unexpected release on a streaming platform.

What was supposed to be Diljit Dosanjh's long-awaited comeback turned into another controversy within 48 hours. Here's why Satluj was pulled from OTT and the true story that made it one of India's most debated films. Diljit Dosanjh's long-delayed film ‘Satluj’ has once again found itself at the centre of controversy. After years of battling certification issues, title changes, and release delays, the film finally premiered on ZEE5 on July 3, 2026 only to be removed from the platform in India less than 48 hours later. The film, directed by Honey Trehan and starring Diljit Dosanjh as slain human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, remains available on ZEE5 Global outside India, while its future domestic release remains uncertain. On July 5, ZEE5 announced that ‘Satluj’ had been taken down from its Indian catalogue, citing only "current developments" without elaborating further.

The title changed more than once because the makers could not secure approval for the original name, Ghallughara, and later the censorship process pushed the film toward the title Punjab 95. After years of delay, the film finally arrived on streaming as Satluj, with Honey Trehan saying the earlier titles could not be retained. He also made it clear that the team refused to release a compromised version. Even after finally releasing on ZEE5 Global, the film was reportedly taken down from the platform in India shortly after it began streaming. That sudden removal sparked fresh discussion about censorship, political pressure and the unresolved conflict surrounding the film’s content. The film had already faced heavy delays, a withdrawn festival premiere, and years of uncertainty before its release.

Diljit Dosanjh plays human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra in Satluj The abrupt removal of a film starring popular Indian singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh from a streaming platform has triggered a row. Satluj is inspired by the life of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, who investigated allegations of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings during Punjab's separatist insurgency - and then he himself disappeared. He was later found to have been abducted and murdered. Several Punjab police officers were eventually convicted for their role in the killing. Satluj was released on the ZEE5 platform on Friday but removed two days later. ZEE5 said in a statemen, externalt the film would be unavailable in India "until further notice" because of "current developments" but did not explain what they were. With ZEE5 pulling it, the film is no longer officially available in India.
